doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Playing Taps on the harmonic series as an embouchure exercise
summary: Playing Taps on low B flat overtones is a good method for intonation and embouchure control, from his Sedola lessons.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: That’s funny. I never heard anybody doing — I guess I remember it in the practice rooms, saxophone players doing that, but I never heard anybody actually do it.

Yeah it’s actually a good method for teaching intonation and embouchure position. That’s part of what I had to do with Sedola was do that kind of a thing and be able to get to the third partial level where you can pretty much play diatonic melodies up in the third partial. And he would have me do this on low B flat, lip slur them with no articulation, which was hard. And eventually just your control of that finite position of your embouchure — because it can make you put your bottom lip over your bottom teeth when you did this. So it was sort of both lips — and it was very hard to do but it really gave you finite control of like how your embouchure opened and closed.
